dag.description: Minimal synchronous Bedrock LLM data-processing / scoring building block. Pre-staged (Dummy-loaded) data is preprocessed and then scored/enriched by BedrockProcessing under a generated prompt template. Terminal — the output is the LLM-processed dataset; no label ruleset, training, packaging, or registration.

cost.estimated_hours: 0.5-4 (synchronous Bedrock inference over the input batch)

agent_context.when_to_use: Run synchronous Bedrock LLM processing (scoring, enrichment, or feature generation) over pre-staged (Dummy-loaded) tabular+text data, gated by a generated prompt template. This is the smallest Bedrock scoring building block and is the rnr_pytorch_bedrock batch-scoring DAG (dag_batch.json) used to produce LLM-processed outputs without any downstream model.
agent_context.when_not_to_use: If you need asynchronous/batch Bedrock throughput, use bedrock_batch_data_processing (BedrockBatchProcessing). If you then apply a label ruleset to derive labels, use bedrock_cradle_label_ruleset_labeling. If you train a model downstream, use a full bedrock end-to-end DAG (bedrock_pytorch_e2e / bedrock_pytorch_with_label_ruleset_e2e).
differentiators: Smallest Bedrock scoring DAG with an explicit BedrockPromptTemplateGeneration node feeding the processing step
Synchronous BedrockProcessing (vs asynchronous BedrockBatchProcessing in bedrock_batch_data_processing)
Terminal — emits LLM-processed data, no training / ruleset / packaging
Dummy/pre-staged input rather than live Cradle SQL

prerequisites.how: BedrockPromptTemplateGeneration produces the template consumed by BedrockProcessing_training
DummyDataLoading_training points at the staged EDX/S3 dataset

common_pitfalls: BedrockProcessing consumes BOTH the TabularPreprocessing output and the generated prompt template
Keep the prompt template schema in sync with the preprocessed columns
For very large populations prefer bedrock_batch_data_processing to avoid synchronous timeouts
